text:
sam: Heads-up — noticed sustained memory drift on long streaming sessions that use tool loops. Repro in staging: memory climbs ~200MB every 10–15 mins until OOM in ~3 hours. attaching quick repro steps below.
priya: ouch. any obvious GC roots or retention in heap profile?
luc: can you paste the exact command you used to repro? trying to run locally.
sam: repro command:```bash
# start a long streaming chat with toolloop invocation every ~30s
python tools/repro_longstream.py --model small --loop-interval 30 --duration 2h
```
maria: I ran that for 45m earlier — saw KV pages go from 48k -> 62k, slab fragments increasing. Posting a few lines from the memprofile:```text
heap_total: 3.2GB
kv_pages: 62345
kv_fragments: 184
open_sessions: 42
live_kv_refs: 42
```
jon: interesting — kv_pages increases even when eviction should trigger. are eviction callbacks firing?
sam: `kv-monitor-bot` shows eviction events, but frequency drops as pages climb. logs: `evict_attempts=120 evicted=0 threshold_pages=60000 reason=locked_refs`
eva: "locked_refs" suggests in-use pointers preventing reclaim. might be the streaming output ring buffer holding onto older KV slices for tool loop retries.
priya: could also be allocation alignment changes in the new kernel or a recent jemalloc update — we bumped allocator to 5.3 last week. any correlating deploys?
luc: looked at deploy timeline — runtime/serving commit 9f3a2 landed just before the bump. that touched kernel selection path but also changed small-allocation codegen.
sam: I ran `pmap` and `smem` snapshots during a run — anonymous mappings for KV steadily increase, but resident set only goes up when we trigger tool loop heavy IO. suspect fragmentation + retained refs.
maria: quick mitigation idea: add a soft reclaim in session tear-down and periodic `kv_cache.trim(age_threshold=30s)` for sessions with repeated tool loops. cheap to try.
jon: agree. let's add a metric `kv_eviction_locked_count` and surface it in console, then run canary with `kv_cache.force_reclaim_on_threshold=true`.
eva: also instrument the ring buffer: add counters for `ring_hold_count` and log backtraces when `ring_hold_count > 5` for >1m. this should catch code paths accidentally retaining refs.
priya: I'll prepare a small patch to add the metrics + a feature flag for force reclaim. canary target: staging-cpu-3, will run 2x of sam's repro and compare memory curves.
sam: thanks. i'll attach the full heap diff and a perf map after the next run. for reference, here's a minimal heap-diff snippet that shows persistent map entries:```text
+map[session_id: 42] -> kv_slice{page=61234, size=8k, refs=3}
+map[session_id: 42] -> kv_slice{page=61235, size=8k, refs=2}
```
luc: one more note — kernel selection change in 9f3a2 introduced a different page-size hint for large allocations (`MADV_HUGEPAGE` toggle). if the allocator chooses mixed page sizes we can see fragmentation and poor reclaim. can we try disabling hugepages in canary?
maria: will add a canary matrix: (a) force_reclaim flag, (b) disable hugepages, (c) jemalloc rollback. run each for 2h and collect `kv_pages`, `kv_fragments`, `rss`, `virtual`.
jon: I'll wire up dashboards and set an alert if `kv_pages` delta > 10k over 30m.
eva: also queue a short flamegraph capture every 15m during repro to see if there are unexpected hot paths holding refs.
sam: appreciate it. next actions: priya patch + feature flag, luc disable hugepages run, maria orchestrate canary matrix, jon dashboard & alert, eva flamegraphs. I'll post the heap diff + full logs after the next run (ETA ~3h). :thumbsup:
kv-monitor-bot: scheduled job started: `mem-drift-repro` on staging-cpu-3, expected run 2h — capturing metrics every 30s.
